summary: Sibraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sibnath Sarma, D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah, and served as Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).

Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844–1884) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Göttingen, and earned his Ph.D. at Tübingen (1867), studying under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He was an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg (1881).

Siegfried Lienhard (1924–2011) was an Indologist who earned his doctorate from Vienna (1949) and habilitated at Stockholm University. He served as professor at Kiel University (1962–1968) and Stockholm University (1968–1990), and as General Secretary of the IASS (~1978–1987).

Siglinde Dietz (b. 1945) is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and scholar of Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn under Michael Hahn in 1980 and held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990).
Signe Cohen specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied under Ludo Rocher and serves as a professor at the University of Missouri.

Signe Howell (1942–2025) was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1973–1974) and the University of Oxford (~1974–1980), and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

Silvio Vita (1954–2023) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology, studying at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton. He served as Director of the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2002–2017) and held a professorship at University of Naples Federico II (~2002–2023).

Simo Parpola (b. 1943) is a linguist and historian who completed his PhD at the University of Helsinki (1968). He served as associate professor at the University of Chicago (1977–1979) and professor at the University of Helsinki beginning in 1978.

Simon P. James is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University as Tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Lecturer in Philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

Singhathon Narasabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti (attested 1971).

Siniruddha Dash is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (2000–2014) and Director of the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 2013).

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist who studied at Cambridge, the University of London, and Harvard under Frank Raymond Allchin. He served as Director General of the Department of Archaeology from circa 1992 to 2001.

Sisir Roy works in philosophy and other fields, having studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at the Indian Statistical Institute as Professor and at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (both attested 2009).
Sister Vajirā (1928–1991) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. She studied under Paul Debes and was taught by Narada Maha Thera in 1955.
Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at The University of Hong Kong. Kwan studied under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Zhihua Yao.

So Takahashi (b. 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed an M.A. at the University of Tokyo. Takahashi held positions at Meijo University as Associate Professor (attested 1977–1978) and Professor (attested 1991).

Sodo Mori (b. 1934) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura, later serving as professor at Josai University (from 1977) and Aichi Gakuin University (1991–2003).
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Antai-ji (1949–1957). He studied under teachers Kodo Sawaki (1949–1957) and Eko Hashimoto.
Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and under traditional teacher Gempo Yamamoto (~1931–1951).

Sogaku Daiun Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University (-1901) under teachers including Sodo Harada and Dokutan Sōsan. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (1911–1923).
